key_insight: Patient-specific preoperative CT can initialize a dynamic Gaussian-splatting scene that models respiratory deformation, enabling accurate CT-to-endoscope registration in real time and removing the need for disruptive breath-hold protocols.
problem_solved: CT-to-body divergence during bronchoscopy caused by respiratory motion (5–20 mm deformations) undermines navigation accuracy and forces clinically disruptive breath-hold workflows.
method: CT-informed initialization: convert preoperative CT into a Gaussian-splatting scene to capture airway geometry and appearance priors.
Patient-specific respiratory deformation: learn or fit a low-dimensional motion model that deforms Gaussians over the breathing cycle so the scene matches intraoperative anatomy.

Real-time registration and rendering: render dynamic endoscopic views from the deformed splatting scene and align live bronchoscope video to the rendered scene for continuous localization without breath-holds.
impact: Combines anatomical priors with neural rendering to enable robust, real-time localization in deforming anatomical environments—reducing reliance on protocol-driven data collection and improving clinical workflow; approach is extensible to other endoscopic or organ-motion settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: CT → Gaussian splats → respiratory deformation → rendered endoscopic view → video registration
Before/after comparison: static CT-registration with large error vs. CT-informed dynamic registration aligned to live bronchoscope frames
Respiration timeline: plot showing breathing phase, modeled deformation, and corresponding registration error decreasing with the dynamic model
Annotated bronchoscope view: overlay of rendered anatomy and registration offsets to show real-time alignment
paper_title: Stop Holding Your Breath: CT-Informed Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Bronchoscopy
paper_authors: Andrea Dunn Beltran, Daniel Rho, Aarav Mehta, Xinqi Xiong, Raúl San José Estépar
